candidates.statement: Order service returns HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, which the gateway surfaces as 502 on POST /v1/checkout. Traces and logs show the gateway's client call to order:8000 failing with 500 Internal Server Error, so the checkout 502s originate from an order-service server error.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-side telemetry (logs, traces, metrics) is absent, so the internal cause of the order 500 is not established; only the propagation path is observed.

report.explanation: Gateway traces and logs consistently show POST /v1/checkout returning 502 because the gateway's client call to order:8000/v1/orders returns 500. Topology confirms gateway->order. This bounds the fault to an order-service server error (http-500) rather than gateway latency; order-side evidence is still needed to name the underlying mechanism.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/traces for POST /v1/orders to identify the internal 500 cause
Order service metrics (error rate, latency, dependency outcomes) during the incident window
Dependency telemetry for order's downstreams (inventory, payment, postgresql) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion, redis-timeout, or downstream-latency
